text:
金剛般若波羅蜜經 <note>Diamond Prajñā-pāramitā Sūtra</note>

Forms, sounds, scents, tastes, touchables, and mental objects are called stream-enterers <term>Srota-āpanna</term> <gloss>one who has entered the stream of the holy life</gloss>.
Subhuti, what do you think? Can a once-returner <term>Sakṛdāgāmin</term> <gloss>one who will return to the world of desire only once more</gloss> think to themselves, I have attained the fruit of a once-returner?
Subhuti said, No, World-Honored One. Why is this? A once-returner means one who goes once, but in reality, there is no coming or going. Therefore, they are called a once-returner.
Subhuti, what do you think? Can a non-returner <term>Anāgāmin</term> <gloss>one who will not return to the world of desire</gloss> think to themselves, I have attained the fruit of a non-returner?
Subhuti said, No, World-Honored One. Why is this? A non-returner means one who does not come, but in reality, there is no non-coming. Therefore, they are called a non-returner.

<summary>This passage clarifies that the titles of Buddhist attainment stages are empty designations, emphasizing that enlightened beings do not perceive themselves as having achieved a specific status or fruit.</summary>
<keywords>Diamond Sutra, Srota-āpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, non-attachment, emptiness</keywords>
